reply_text:
Read the three commits on the `claude/lean4-python-diagramprover-review-kytnxq` branch. Now checking whether the branch merges cleanly.㊥ (the three commits) I've read them. They are on the branch `origin/claude/lean4-python-diagramprover-review-kytnxq`, not on master. The branch sits directly on top of current master, so merging would be a fast-forward. Of the three, `f7ba3a34` connects most directly to M-象-2000. Its `skeleton/xiang2000.clj` writes five patterns as small causal models with declared inputs and outputs, and joins them into the Kimi red-tape incident of 2026-09-24, which is M-象-2000's acceptance case. It then computes answers to questions the mission had left open or answered by hand.

㊢ (what the skeleton computes)
- **Derivation of R.** The report → constrain → propose chain comes out as the set of causes of the commit. The mission had reconstructed this by hand from session order.
- **The `:反事实世界模型` hole.** If the guard pattern had been in force, there would have been no red tape. The joined pattern models serve as the world model that ARGUE-0 said was missing.
- **Withdrawal semantics.** The two possible wirings give different answers. Under the gate as built, which never reads rule records, withdrawing the rule record leaves the red tape in place. If enforcement read the record, withdrawing it would stop the red tape.
- **The capture drop.** It comes out causally independent of the requisition commit. That holds only for these five patterns; adding a pattern that links them would change it.
- **103 implied independencies.** These are predictions the act history could falsify. None has been tested yet.

㊟ (limits it states itself) The models are written from the mission's text, not mined from the store. Values are true/false only, with no probabilities. Variables are matched by name. I haven't run its tests. The commit reports 71 tests passing and four planted bugs caught.

🈖 (relation to M-aif-over-the-operator and today's MAP)
- **Withdrawal.** The withdrawal result is the same distinction our mission draws between a `:withdrawn` record and what the machine actually does. A record can change what gets reported without changing what gets enforced.
- **Two other routes to patterns.** Its item "Patterns that predict" turns each flexiarg into a causal model whose independencies can be tested against the act history. Our pattern-bidding route found that patterns barely line up with operator turns, which is part of why we went to keywords. This is a different route: it tests patterns against what happened, not against what you said.
- **S8 and offers.** S8 would join an arriving act into the model before it lands. That fits the offer pipeline: an offer with an action class is exactly such an arriving act.

㊭ (next step) If you want it in the running system, merge the branch to master (fast-forward) and reload from there. That follows the one-JVM rule, and nothing is lost by waiting. I've left the branch alone.
